intro: Sequence questions give a long row of numbers or letters and ask you to count the places that fit a rule, like "an even number just after a prime".

tips.title: Read the rule word by word
tips.body: "Immediately after" means the very next place. "Between" means one on each side. "Not immediately followed by" rules some places out.

tips.title: Mark, then count
tips.body: Go through the row once, from left to right, and mark each place that fits. Then count the marks. Counting in your head is where mistakes creep in.

tips.title: Know the special numbers
tips.body: Primes under 10: 2, 3, 5, 7 (1 is not prime). Squares: 0, 1, 4, 9. Factors of 4: 1, 2, 4. Vowels: A, E, I, O, U.

tips.title: Overlaps count
tips.body: In 3 6 9, both 3 6 and 6 9 are pairs that differ by 3. Don't skip a number just because it was part of the last match.

tips.title: Positions
tips.body: For "the 6th letter to the left of the 8th", find the 8th first, then count 6 back: 8 − 6 = the 2nd letter.
